lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The giant's head was carried to Jerusalem and David's fame spread through every tribe. Saul summoned the young man to live at his side.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The people sang in the streets. Saul's own spear lay across his knees while David's hand was near the king's.

lines.speaker: saul
lines.text: They have given him ten thousands, and me only thousands. What more can he want but the kingdom?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An evil spirit troubled Saul. When the music of a lyre rose from the palace, the shadow on his face lifted for a moment.

lines.speaker: saul
lines.text: Play for me, David. The noise in my head is louder tonight.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I will play, my king. But the music is not the cure. It only holds the dark at bay.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David played, and Saul's hand steadied. But the king watched the musician with a look that was not gratitude.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Saul's jealousy grew with David's honour. The spear that once defended the king became the thing he lifted against the lyre-player.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: What have I done? Is there not a cause for this spear?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David fled the palace that night. The anointed shepherd left the king's house with nothing but the echo of a song.

choices.label: Run before the spear finds me 🏃
choices.note: Survival first. The calling can wait for safer ground.

choices.label: Stay and face the king 🛡️
choices.note: A servant's trust does not leave when the master is afraid.
